item.title: Fresh Prep gets court approval to buy fellow meal kit company Goodfood
item.description: Canadian meal delivery company Fresh Prep Foods Inc. says it has received court permission to acquire distressed competitor Goodfood Market Corp.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: Canadian meal delivery company Fresh Prep Foods Inc. says it has received court permission to acquire distressed competitor Goodfood Market Corp. Fresh Prep refused to disclose how much it will pay for Goodfood but says the deal is expected to close on or around Friday. Once the deal closes, Fresh Prep says it will begin serving about 30,000 Goodfood customers. Goodfood filed for creditor protection with the Superior Court of Quebec over the summer in hopes of restructuring under a new owner or with help from investors. The Montreal-based company started in 2014 and is known for selling pre-measured sets of ingredients and recipes to customers who cook them into meals. Fresh Prep operates similarly. It was founded in Vancouver in 2015 and acquired another Montreal-based meal kit company called Cook It Recipes Inc. in 2024. --- Tara Deschamps, The Canadian Press This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 10, 2026.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（10日）
item.description: ＜ロンドン株式市場＞ まちまちで取引を終えた。金価格の反落を受け、貴金属株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反落した。一...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（10日） 4:34 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞　まちまちで取引を終えた。金価格の反落を受け、貴金属株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は小幅に反落した。一方、中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．１６％続伸した。    ＦＴＳＥ３５０種貴金属株指数は４．７２％安。貴金属採掘フレスニヨは４．７％、エンデバー・マイニングは４．３％、銅大手アントファガスタは２．１％いずれも下落した。    石油・ガス株指数は１．６７％安。トランプ米大統領がイランへの軍事攻撃を当面見送る姿勢を示したことを受け、北海ブレント原油先物価格は節目の１バレル＝９０ドルを一時割り込んだ。    一方、飲料株指数は０．８７％、生活必需品株指数は０．７４％それぞれ上昇。小売り大手マークス・アンド・スペンサー（Ｍ＆Ｓ）は４．１％高だった。    イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）のロンバルデリ副総裁は、１２月会合での利上げの可能性を排除しないとの見解を示した。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では１２月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げが決まる可能性を約５０％と見込んでいる。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞　続伸して取引を終えた。米イラン間の軍事衝突への懸念が後退し、原油先物価格が下落したことが投資家心理を後押しした。米国株と比べて欧州株に相対的な割安感が出ていることも、投資家が資金を振り向けやすい環境になっているとの指摘もある。    ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数は１．６８％上昇した。銀行株の比重が大きいスペインのＩＢＥＸ指数は０．９８％高だった。    米当局がイランに対する大規模な軍事作戦の必要性に否定的な見方を示したことを受け、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種石油・ガス株指数は１．６０％下落した。    フランスの決済プラットフォーム、エデンレッドは６．４％上昇。ブラジルでの司法判断を受け、買われた。    ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、欧州の主要企業の２０２６年第３・四半期（２６年７－９月期）の利益は約２５％増と、従来予想約１６％増を上回る見込みだ。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞　国債利回りが上昇した。米インフレ指標が予想を上回ったことで米国債利回りが上昇したことに追随した。    ドイツの２年債利回りは６ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇して３．０７％となり、１日の上昇幅としては１カ月ぶりの大きさとなる見通し。ユーロ圏の指標となる１０年債利回りは３ｂｐ上昇して３．３０％となった。    いずれも欧州時間の午前中の取引では低下していたが、１０月の米消費者物価（ＣＰＩ）が前月比０．４％上昇と予想を上回る伸びを示し、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が来月利上げする軌道にあることが示されたことを受け、上昇に転じた。nL6N46R141    これを受けて米２年債利回りは１６ｂｐ上昇、指標の１０年債利回りは１２ｂｐ上昇して４．９９％となった。    リーガン・キャピタルの最高投資責任者（ＣＩＯ）、スカイラー・ウェイナンド氏は、今回のデータについて「ＦＲＢが明らかなインフレ加速を無視できないことは明白であり、１２月の追加利上げの下地が整った」と述べた。    米インフレ指標の上振れが欧州経済に直接波及するわけではないが、米国債の動きが他の市場に波及することは多い。    その他のユーロ圏国債利回りも、米インフレ指標を受けて上昇した。    フランスの１０年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇して４．７８％となった。序盤には、エネルギー価格の下落を受けて一時約６ｂｐ低下する場面もあった。    イタリアの１０年債利回りも同程度上昇し、４．３５％となった。

ユーロ圏金融・債券市場：[DE/BJ]

FAST

Nov 10 : Nscale, a British cloud provider backed by chip giant Nvidia, is considering delaying a $35 billion stock market listing, the Telegraph reported on Tuesday. Executives at the data-centre developer are assessing whether to pause efforts to go public until next year, the report added. Nscale did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The report comes days after Reuters reported that Microsoft had declined an option to expand its existing agreement with Nscale to rent more computing power at a Texas data center.

The London-based company filed for an IPO in September, when it sought about $3.5 billion in funding, including $2 billion from Nvidia. Nscale plans to list on the NYSE under the symbol "NSCL." The news about Nscale's IPO comes as Anthropic moves ahead with its own listing plans. The AI giant on Tuesday filed an updated prospectus for its IPO, seeking a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, slightly short of some investors' expectations. Anthropic's IPO is seen as a key test of Wall Street's faith in the AI boom it helped ignite.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Bank of Canada moving carefully, but further hikes might be needed: meeting summary
item.description: The Bank of Canada’s governing council thinks it might need to raise interest rates further, but it’s proceeding carefully, according to a summary of deliberations.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: OTTAWA — The Bank of Canada’s governing council thinks it might need to raise interest rates further, but it’s proceeding carefully, according to a summary of deliberations of its recent decision to raise its key policy rate for the first time since 2023. According to the report, the council acknowledged it faced considerable uncertainty and said it would take its monetary policy decisions one meeting at a time. The Bank of Canada raised its policy interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 2.5 per cent last month to reduce the risk that stubbornly high oil prices become persistent inflation. The summary says the council members agreed that monetary policy cannot lower global energy prices, but can prevent them from leading to generalized inflation. The decision came as the Bank of Canada raised its outlook for the annual inflation rate to hit 3.5 per cent at the end of this year and remain above three per cent for much of 2027. The summary of deliberations said higher costs largely haven’t been passed through to consumers so far, but the bank’s surveys suggest businesses expect to raise some prices over the next year. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 10, 2026.

FAST

Nov 10 : South Africa's twice Olympic gold medallist Tatjana Smith is changing her allegiance to the Netherlands, the 29-year-old said on Tuesday, citing her Dutch heritage and greater opportunities for high-performance support. • Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, retired in 2024 but reversed her decision earlier this year with her sights on the LA28 Games • "To South Africa, when I was a little girl, my biggest dream was to represent my country at the Olympics," Smith said in a tearful video statement posted to social media. "I got to live that dream and it gave me more than I could have ever imagined" • Smith, the 200 metres breaststroke gold medallist in Tokyo and 100m breaststroke champion at the Paris Games, holds dual citizenship with the Netherlands. She has said financial difficulties had made her swimming career hard to sustain • "This gives me the opportunity to explore another part of my identity and the heritage that I've never experienced through sport," said Smith, who also has two Olympic silvers. "The opportunity also offers greater high performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career"

Source: Reuters

item.title: Google’s Gemini Targets Health Care’s Data Problem
item.description: Google Cloud is launching Gemini for Health Care, an AI platform designed to connect fragmented information across hospitals, insurers and other health systems while reducing administrative work. item.title: Boeing recibe 165 pedidos de aviones en octubre, su mejor registro para ese mes desde 1997
item.description: Las sólidas cifras de pedidos respaldan las afirmaciones de los ejecutivos del sector de que la demanda de aviones nuevos y más eficientes en el consumo de combustible sigue siendo fuerte.
item.dc:creator: Will Guisbond
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Boeing Co. ( BA ) registró su mejor octubre en pedidos de aviones comerciales en casi 30 años, una señal de la demanda sostenida de nuevos aviones incluso cuando los altos precios del combustible para aviones están afectando a sus clientes de aerolíneas. La compañía consiguió 165 pedidos netos el mes pasado, la mayor cantidad después de cancelaciones en un mes de octubre desde 1997. La mayoría procedían del arrendador Avolon Holdings Ltd. para 140 aviones 737 Max 10, lo que eleva la cartera de pedidos para la variante más grande del 737 a casi 1.700 aeronaves, apenas unas semanas después de obtener la aprobación del regulador estadounidense. Ver más: Boeing recortará el 5% de los empleos de su división comercial en medio de ajustes de producción Las sólidas cifras de pedidos respaldan las afirmaciones de los ejecutivos del sector de que la demanda de aviones nuevos y más eficientes en el consumo de combustible sigue siendo fuerte, a pesar de que las aerolíneas se enfrentan a unos precios del combustible más elevados derivados del conflicto entre EE.UU. e Irán. Al mismo tiempo, las entregas del 737 Max cayeron a su nivel más bajo en casi un año, con 32 entregas en octubre, tal y como informó anteriormente Bloomberg . El mes pasado, el CEO, Kelly Ortberg, comunicó a los inversores que unos problemas de proceso estaban obstaculizando la producción de alas, lo que retrasaba el aumento de la producción de este popular avión de fuselaje estrecho. Boeing también afirmó que no alcanzaría sus objetivos de entrega para todo el año de los modelos 737 y 787 Dreamliner, y recientemente anunció planes para recortar un 5% de la plantilla de su división de aviones comerciales, en medio de los retrasos en el aumento de la producción. El fabricante de aviones entregó 11.787 en octubre, un resultado más sólido tras haber entregado cuatro en agosto y ocho en septiembre. El total de entregas mensuales asciende a 49 aviones. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: World shares rise after technology shares advance on Wall Street ahead of U.S. inflation data
item.description: Global markets were higher Tuesday after U.S. stocks rallied, recovering most of their big losses from last week, while investors awaited U.S. inflation data for October.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — U.S. stocks are falling Tuesday after a report showed inflation was worse across the country last month than economists expected. The S&P 500 fell 0.9 per cent and gave back some of its big rally from the day before. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 319 points, or 0.6 per cent, as of 1:29 p.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 1.4 per cent lower. Pressure from the bond market undercut stocks following the discouraging report on inflation. People had to pay prices for groceries, electricity and other costs of living that were even higher last month than economists expected. That could push the Federal Reserve to hike its main interest rate at its next meeting in December and beyond. Higher interest rates can help rein in inflation, but they do so by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money and by slowing the overall economy. Higher rates also make investors less willing to pay high prices for stocks and other investments. One Fed official even hinted the central bank may increase the federal funds rate by double the typical amount next month because of how high inflation has remained for years. Speaking in London before the inflation report was released, Fed Gov. Christopher Waller said “a stronger policy move may be needed” if the report showed an important underlying measure of inflation rose by 0.3 per cent from September. In that case, he said the Fed should consider hiking the federal funds rate by half a percentage point rather than the typical quarter point. Moving by only the usual amount could “put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Shortly afterward, Tuesday’s inflation report showed that the underlying measure of inflation Waller was worried about was exactly 0.3 per cent, the threshold he had set. It’s the Fed’s job to keep inflation under control, along with keeping the job market strong. That sent yields jumping in the bond market as traders upped their forecasts for coming hikes to rates by the Fed. The yield on the 10-year Treasury jumped to 5.01 per cent from 4.88 per cent late Monday. It’s a notable move for the bond market, and the yield helps set where rates are for mortgages and other loans going to U.S. households and businesses. The 10-year Treasury yield had been dropping since early October, when it topped 5.30 per cent as worries spiked about high inflation, higher interest rates, the U.S. government’s big debt and other concerns. Tuesday’s jump in yields came even though oil prices fell again. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil fell 0.8 per cent to US$91.81. U.S. President Donald Trump said late Monday that the war in Iran, which sent oil prices much higher, “militarily is effectively over.” Brent’s price has been falling from more than US$112 at the start of the month amid uncertainty about what will happen with the war with Iran. Jumps in Treasury yields push downward on prices for all kinds of stocks, and they can particularly hurt companies in the real-estate business. Higher mortgage rates can keep potential customers away from homebuilders, for example, and Lennar fell 4.4 per cent for one of the sharper losses in the S&P 500. Rival homebuilders also fell, including drops of 3.6 per cent for D.R. Horton and 3.5 per cent for PulteGroup. Builders FirstSource, which sells crown mouldings, cabinets and other products to homebuilders, sank 3.9 per cent. The single heaviest weight on the S&P 500 was Nvidia, which fell 6.3 per cent. It’s been under pressure since its board announced an investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, who admitted to a relationship with a woman who, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for China. It’s also been swinging amid broader worries that have knocked the artificial-intelligence industry around recently. Democratic victories in statehouses across the country last week raised concerns about possible restrictions on construction of AI data centres. That built on top of already longstanding worries that AI stock prices had shot too high and were in a bubble. Other stocks in the AI industry also slipped. GE Vernova, which is helping to power AI data centres, dropped 7 per cent. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers, fell 3.6 per cent after flipping between gains and losses earlier in the morning. CoreWeave, a company that rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, fell 2.6 per cent. Advanced Micro Devices held up better and was mostly unchanged. The recent shakiness for AI-related stocks had raised questions about whether Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, may delay its initial public offering of stock. But Anthropic said in a filing with U.S. regulators on Tuesday that it’s looking to sell its stock at a price valuing the company at roughly US$1.3 trillion. That would make it one of the most valuable companies on Wall Street, worth more than Walmart, JPMorgan Chase, ExxonMobil or Coca-Cola. In stock markets abroad, indexes rose across much of Europe and Asia. South Korea’s Kospi jumped 4.4 per cent for one of the world’s biggest gains on strength for its two tech giants that have benefited from the AI boom, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Writers Elaine Lai and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

item.title: 再送-ロシア、ウクライナ10州の送電網攻撃 冬控えエネルギー施設標的
item.description:
(第１段落の州の表記を修正して再送しました)
[１０日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
(第１段落の州の表記を修正して再送しました)

[１０日 ロイター] -  ウクライナのポルタワ、ドニプロペトロウスクなど１０州がロシア軍による攻撃を受け、広範囲にわたり停電が発生した。ウクライナ当局者らが１０日、明らかにした。主要変電所５カ所が標的となり、２人が死亡したという。冬を控える中、ロシアによるエネルギー施設を狙った空爆作戦の一環とみられる。

ロシアとウクライナは今年２月以来となる米仲介による協議を１０－１１日にアラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）の首都アブダビで開催している。

ウクライナのコレツキー首相は通信アプリ「テレグラム」で、ビンニツァ、キロボフラードも含めた各州の変電所がロシア軍による攻撃を受けたと投稿。これに先立ち、ウクライナ国営電力会社ウクレネルゴは、ロシアが夜から朝にかけてウクライナ８州のエネルギーインフラを攻撃し、キーウ、ハルキウ、ドニプロペトロウスクなど６州の家庭で停電が発生したと発表した。

ロシアはここ数カ月、物流施設を含む経済への打撃を狙った空爆を強めている。キロボフラード州の知事によると、大手ホームセンターなどの民間インフラも攻撃を受けた。ドニプロペトロウスク州当局によると、ドローン（無人機）による攻撃があったという。

ウクライナは、弾道ミサイルやジェット推進型無人機を迎撃する兵器不足に直面しており、ロシアの攻撃阻止が課題となっている。

Explainer-Ice hockey-From Canada to Germany, what stands in the way of Russia's ice hockey return?

FAST

Nov 10 : Norway have announced their exclusion from the 2027 World Junior Championship, making way for Russia, despite Canada, the host nation, stating it will bar the Russian team from entering the tournament. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ordered ice hockey's governing body on October 30 to admit Russian teams to five championships. Host governments still decide who can enter, and eight of the 16 teams in the men's World Championship say they would refuse to play Russia. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), now led by Germany's Franz Reindl, said it disagrees with the ruling but will comply. CAS found insufficient evidence that security risks justified extending the ban imposed after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said it had been subsequently informed by the IIHF that Norway would be replaced by Russia at the upcoming junior championship as the lowest-ranked team.

The International Olympic Committee on July 7 provisionally lifted its suspension of the Russian Olympic Committee and withdrew its recommended restrictions on Russian athletes and teams. It had already urged federations to readmit Russian and Belarusian juniors to individual and team events. Here are the details. WHAT COMES NEXT? As of November 10, the IIHF had yet to announce Norway's relegation publicly. Swiss Ice Hockey said it had received a revised schedule naming Russia. In a statement, the federation said it was consulting with national associations, host authorities, and organisers on how to proceed following the court decision. Sweden has urged the European Commission to tighten visa rules for athletes representing Russia or Belarus. Finland is preparing restrictions on short-term work visas for Russian athletes across sports, Finnish broadcaster Yle reported. CAN RUSSIA ENTER THE HOST COUNTRIES? CAS left open whether Russia could play under a neutral flag. Canadian Sports Secretary Adam van Koeverden, however, said the neutral designation applied to individual athletes. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada will not let ice hockey players from Russia or Belarus take part in the World Junior Championship in Alberta in December. Czech Interior Minister Lubomir Metnar said existing rules prevent him from issuing short-stay visas for Russian players for January's women's under-18 championship in Ostrava. Germany's government said opposition from teams and sponsors made staging the men's championship in May with Russia "effectively impossible". Berlin left open the possibility of refusing visas, saying it would assess applications individually. WHICH TEAMS WOULD REFUSE TO FACE RUSSIA? Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Latvia, Norway and Sweden say they would refuse to play Russia. Ukraine qualified for the men's top division for the first time since 2007. Sports Minister Matvii Bidnyi said they intend to compete but would refuse to play Russia.  Switzerland said their juniors will compete in Alberta but would sit out the December 27 game against Russia on the IIHF's revised schedule. HOW HAS RUSSIA RESPONDED? Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday that countries opposing rulings to allow Russia to take part in international sport are violating the rights of both Russian athletes and democratic institutions. Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyarev told Vesti that expecting Russia to withdraw was "the height of hysteria". He called what he described as Swedish fears of psychological trauma "simply idiotic" and said Russia would prove their superiority on the ice. Degtyarev said opponents would forfeit and countries blocking Russia risked losing hosting rights, which the IIHF council can withdraw after a review. He said Moscow would ask the IOC to monitor Canada and Germany. WHY ARE BELARUS STILL EXCLUDED? The CAS ruling covered Russia alone. Belarus have been excluded since the country supported Moscow's invasion. On November 7, the IIHF confirmed Belarus would miss the junior and men's championships, citing existing tournament arrangements. Belarusian federation chairman Alexander Bogdanovich questioned the different treatment. WHAT IS AT STAKE FOR HOSTS AND SPONSORS? The Finnish city of Turku said it will give up co-hosting the 2028 World Juniors in Finland with Tampere if Russia compete. AJ Products, a men's championship sponsor since 1989, has withdrawn from the 2027 tournament. If Russia play, Nokian Tyres will end its sponsorship, Skoda Auto will review its involvement and Strauss will remove its logos while considering a full withdrawal. item.title: Gold price falls nearly 3% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
item.description: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Gold prices fell nearly 3% on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields while reinforcing expectations of a bigger interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve this year. Spot gold XAU= was down 2.8% at $4,021.36 per ounce by 11:33 a.m. ET (1635 GMT). US gold futures GCcv1 for December delivery fell 1.9% to $4,036.00 per ounce. “I think it’s a bit of a short-term negative for gold because the inflation numbers were running a little higher than expected,” said Edward Meir, an analyst at Marex. The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month after advancing 0.6% in September, the Labor Department’s Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast a 0.3% month-on-month rise. Bets on a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December started to build after the inflation print and comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support more aggressive action in the event of a too-hot Consumer Price Index report. The probability of a 25 bp hike is fully priced in, while the possibility of a 50 bp hike rose to 10.5% from 0% before the data, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. The US dollar .DXY rose against a basket of other major currencies, and Treasury yields climbed. A stronger dollar makes gold more expensive for overseas buyers, while higher Treasury yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. “(Gold) continues to trade above the critical $4,000/oz mark,” Standard Chartered said in a note, adding “crude oil, inflation risks and equity markets continue to set the tone of trading for gold with a focus on rate hike expectations for the December Fed meeting.” Meanwhile, the Monetary Authority of Singapore said it would launch a vaulting service to hold bullion for foreign central banks and lower taxes on some companies in the gold market as it competes for a bigger slice of the precious metals trade. Spot silver XAG= fell 3.9% to $51.32 per ounce and palladium XPD= was down 2.0% at $1,021.22. (Reporting by Vedika Thorat and Anjana Anil in Bengaluru; Editing by Kirsten Donovan and Jonathan Ananda)

US skips UN human rights review, drawing criticism

The meeting was postponed until January after Washington refused to take part, saying participation would imply support for the UN Human Rights Council.

The empty seat of the US delegation, during the 60th session of the Human Rights Council, at the European headquarters of the United Nations in Geneva, Switzerland, Sep 8, 2025. (Photo: AP/Salvatore Di Nolfi)

GENEVA: The Un ited States spurned a UN meeting on Tuesday (Nov 10) where its human rights record un der US President Donald Trump was due to be examined, drawing criticism from rights groups who say violations have surged to levels not seen in decades. Washington disengaged from the Geneva-based UN Human Rights Co un cil last year, citing an anti-Israel bias, and this is the second year in a row that it has skipped its own review - a process that even authoritarian state s take part in. The US left its seat on the stage of the UN meeting empty and the council decided to postpone the event until January. A US State Department spokesperson said participation would imply endorsement of the co un cil's work.

"This irredeemable body makes a mockery of human rights through consistent failures to uphold its own 'values' as it p us hes anti-American rhetoric," the spokesperson said, without responding to allegations about the US record. The 47-member co un cil has not directly criticised Washington's rights record but its appointed experts have, such as over migrant deportations. Washington said deportations wer e carried out in accordance with US immigration law.

QUESTIONS ON ABORTION AND DEATH PENALTY The Un iversal Periodic Review asks all 193 UN member states to submit a rights report every few years and these are review ed by other states , which provide non-binding recommendations. UN documents show co un tries had planned on Tuesday to raise issues such as abortion and the death penalty. US and international non-governmental organisations also sent nearly 200 UN submissions covering topics from migration to racial discrimination. “We've seen attacks on f un damental human rights and civil liberties un precedented in generations," Jamil Dakwar , of the American Civil Liberties Un ion , told reporters in Geneva. "Enough is enough." Fourteen co un tries are due to take part in the review process in Geneva this month. In Trump's first term in office, the US submitted its UPR report. Noor Abdalla, wife of pro-Palestinian student activist Mahmoud Khalil, who was held in immigration detention last year, is among campaigners pressing UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk to promptly hold a briefing on the US rights situation, even in Washington's absence. "When the most powerful government in the world is not held acco un table, they think that they can do whatever they want," Abdalla told reporters. However, diplomats were sceptical given that few states want to confront Washington. "The view is to leave the door open and hope they come back in two years," said a diplomat.

item.description: ドイツ銀、ＦＲＢの27年1月追加利上げを予想 Reuters

item.title: ドイツ銀、ＦＲＢの27年1月追加利上げを予想
item.description: [１０日 ロイター] - ドイツ銀行は１０日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が２０２７年１月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ドイツ銀、ＦＲＢの27年1月追加利上げを予想 3:26 配信

2015年12月16日、ワシントンの米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）。REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque/File Photo（ロイター） [１０日 ロイター] - ドイツ銀行は１０日、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が２０２７年１月に２５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の追加利上げを実施するとの見通しを示した。１０月のインフレ指標が予想を上回り、利上げ観測が強まったことを受けた。

ドイツ銀は「今日発表された消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）は引き続き幅広い項目で上昇を示し、物価上昇圧力の根強さについてこれまで抱いていた懸念を強める内容となった」と指摘した。

従来はＦＲＢが１２月と２７年３月に利上げすると予想していた。

労働省発表の１０月のＣＰＩは前月比０．４％上昇。伸びはロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想の０．３％を上回った。９月は０．６％上昇していた。変動の大きい食品とエネルギーを除くコアＣＰＩは前月比０．３％上昇。エコノミスト予想は０．２％上昇だった。nL6N46R141

ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、市場が織り込む１２月の利上げ確率はほぼ９９％となっている。

こうした中、ＦＲＢのウォラー理事は１０日、米国の１０月のインフレ率が鈍化したとしてもＦＲＢは１２月の会合で利上げを支持する考えを示し、物価情勢が悪化した場合は０．５％ポイントの大幅利上げを検討する必要があると述べた。 nL6N46R11A

これに対しドイツ銀は「ウォラー理事の発言は、１２月に５０ｂｐ利上げする可能性を示した。われわれもその可能性は排除しないが、利上げ幅の拡大は基本シナリオではない」と述べた。

item.title: US CPI Exceeds Expectations Again, Waller's Warning Comes True! Wall Street Focuses on Whether December Rate Hike Will Be 25 or 50 Basis Points; "New Fed News Agency": Stop-and-Go Strategy Faces Test
item.description: The "New Federal Reserve Newsletter" pointed out that before the release of the CPI, Waller suggested the possibility of a 50-basis-point rate hike in December, and so far, no other Fed officials have publicly responded. In addition to a single 50-basis-point hike, the Fed may also choose to signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. Wall Street generally believes that inflationary pressures remain stubborn, further strengthening the case for a rate hike in December, though a 50-basis-point increase is not a consensus. The market is concerned about whether the Fed will extend the tightening cycle.
item.dc:creator: 华尔街见闻
item.content:encoded: US inflation in October once again exceeded expectations, further raising market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December, with the possibility of a larger rate increase now being discussed. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) announced on Tuesday, November 10, that the October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month, lower than the 0.6% increase in September but higher than economists’ forecasts of 0.3%. The core CPI rose 0.3% month-on-month, matching September’s increase and exceeding the market’s expectation of 0.2%. This marks the third consecutive month where overall CPI rose more than Wall Street predicted, and core CPI has also climbed 0.3% month-on-month for three straight months. Due to the failure to collect CPI data during the US federal government shutdown in October 2025, the BLS was unable to provide a year-on-year figure for October CPI. This report precisely meets the policy threshold previously outlined by Federal Reserve Governor Waller. Just hours before the CPI was published, Waller stated that if the core CPI for October increased by 0.3% or more month-on-month, he might support a 50 basis point rate hike at the Fed’s monetary policy meeting in December. With this criterion now met, the market’s bets on a 50 basis point rate hike in December have gained momentum. Nick Timiraos, a journalist nicknamed the “New Fed Whisperer,” pointed out that this inflation report is testing the Fed’s previous strategy of “spacing out rate hikes,” using staggered moves to leave room to monitor economic data. The choices facing policymakers are not only between a 25 or 50 basis point hike in December, but also whether to adjust the pace of subsequent actions, or even to signal back-to-back rate hikes in December and January of next year. Wall Street’s reaction is showing a common assessment: inflationary pressures remain stubborn, providing more justification for a December rate hike, though opinions differ on the size of the increase. Some believe that three consecutive months of core CPI climbing 0.3% makes it difficult for the Fed to ignore the inflation rebound; others feel that a 50-basis-point hike may be too aggressive and that 25 basis points is still the more realistic option. The market’s real concern is not just the decision at the next meeting but also whether the Fed may extend the tightening cycle as a result. “New Fed Whisperer”: Core prices strengthen across the board, Fed could signal back-to-back hikes In his analysis in The Wall Street Journal, Timiraos noted that the strong showing of October inflation is testing the Fed’s strategy of spreading out rate hikes across different meetings to allow time to observe economic data. He noted that Waller has raised the possibility that if the third month’s inflation data remains hot, a 50-basis-point rate hike in December could be on the table. However, no other Fed officials have publicly echoed this position as of yet. The Fed could also choose another way to address inflationary pressures: instead of a one-off 50-basis-point increase at a single meeting, it could signal consecutive rate hikes in December and January. According to Timiraos, this could be one way to adjust the policy pace. The last time the Fed raised rates by more than 25 basis points at once was back in 2022. On social media, Timiraos further broke down the details of core inflation, pointing out that core prices “strengthened broadly” in October. Specifically, core goods prices rose at a 1% annualized pace over the past six months, compared with just 0.1% in the previous period through June; core services prices excluding shelter rose 0.4% in October, about 4.9% annualized, while three- and six-month annualized increases stood at 5.5% and 3.2% respectively. He also pointed out that the unrounded month-on-month increase in core CPI for October was 0.296%, marking the third straight month at about 0.3%. The three-month annualized rate for core CPI climbed to 3.75%, compared with only 1.6% in July. This data shows that inflationary pressures are not just driven by overall energy price increases—core goods and services prices are also consistently strengthening. For the Fed, this makes it harder to treat inflation as a short-term shock and simply wait for price pressures to subside on their own. Waller raises 50-basis-point option, market begins to reassess policy strength Just hours before the CPI was released, Waller gave a hawkish speech while attending an event in London. He said the US economy was experiencing strong growth and a stable labor market, but inflation remained too high, requiring the Fed to “tighten policy sooner rather than later.” Waller had previously supported the Fed’s decision to keep rates unchanged at the last meeting, arguing that previous policy communications had already led financial markets to price in some degree of tightening. He believes policy adjustments do not have to be implemented in consecutive meetings, but prior guidance on rate hikes must eventually be delivered on, otherwise markets may lower expectations for further tightening, causing financial conditions to ease prematurely. Regarding the December meeting, Waller had already indicated before the CPI was published that if the October core CPI once again rose by around 0.3% month-on-month (as in the previous two months) or even higher, more forceful policy action might be needed. He explicitly raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point hike, and warned that if inflation remained high and price pressures broadened, raising rates by only 25 basis points could hurt the Fed’s credibility in fighting inflation. Ultimately, the October core CPI met this threshold. According to Reuters, after the data was announced, market expectations for a 25-basis-point rate hike in December were almost certain, and bets on a 50-basis-point hike rose to about 15% at one point. The two-year US Treasury yield surged, recording its largest single-day rise since early April 2025. However, Timiraos also cautioned that no other Fed official has publicly echoed Waller’s 50-basis-point position so far. Thus, the market’s discussion of a larger rate hike does not necessarily mean consensus within the Fed. Wall Street divided: Inflation pressures cannot be ignored, but 50 basis points is not a consensus After the inflation data was released, several Wall Street figures said the reasons for a December Fed rate hike had increased, but assessments of the scale and the persistence of inflation pressures varied. Omair Sharif, President of Inflation Insights, commented that the latest report “offers little to ease market concerns about persistent inflation risks” and does not dispel the Fed’s reasons for further hikes. He also estimated that the October core PCE price index might climb by 0.34%, representing an annualized increase of over 4%, higher than the previous month. While the Fed’s 2% policy target is based on headline PCE inflation, core PCE better reflects the underlying inflation trend. If this estimate is confirmed by subsequent data, it would further justify Fed tightening. James McCann, Senior Economist at Edward Jones, described this as another “disappointing inflation report,” reflecting that underlying price pressures may be building again. With US economic growth and the labor market both clearly accelerating this year, and core inflation showing signs of reacceleration, the Fed faces even greater policy pressure. McCann pointed out that the real worry is whether inflation is settling at a higher level. He argued the report at least solidifies the rationale for a 25-basis-point hike in December, while the bigger debate has become whether the Fed needs a 50-basis-point hike and more aggressive action. Peter Cardillo, Chief Market Economist at Spartan Capital Securities, also believes a December rate hike is virtually certain, with the suspense lying in whether it will be 25 or 50 basis points. He commented that Waller has effectively paved the way for a half-point hike, and the latest data shows inflation remains an issue. However, Cardillo also cautioned that circumstances could still change over the next 30 to 40 days. Should oil prices retreat and pass through to consumer prices, inflationary pressures may ease; but if oil rebounds, the inflation outlook could deteriorate again. Chris Zaccarelli, Chief Investment Officer at Northlight Asset Management, believes inflation above an ideal level further increases the likelihood of a December Fed hike. Still, despite market calls for a 50-basis-point hike, he expects the Fed will only lift rates by 25 basis points next month. Joe Saluzzi, Co-Head of Themis Trading, likewise noted that persistently high core inflation shows that price pressures have “stickiness” and that a 25-basis-point hike remains realistic, while 50 basis points may be too aggressive. He also warned that prolonged high rates and inflation will continue to pressure borrowing-dependent businesses, affecting profits and stock valuations. Skyler Weinand, Chief Investment Officer at Regan Capital, stated that the latest CPI paves the way for another Fed rate hike in December—the central bank cannot ignore the clear rebound in inflation data. He also pointed out that the latest jobs report showed robust employment gains in October as well as upward revisions to previous months’ data, providing the Fed with more room for further hikes. Labor market remains resilient, tightening policies may persist longer Besides inflation itself, the continued resilience of the US labor market also provides the Fed more leeway to prioritize combating inflation in its policy decisions. In his speech on Tuesday, Waller noted that US unemployment fell to 4.1% in October, with 165,000 new jobs added that month and a combined upward revision of 85,000 jobs over the prior two months. Although the average monthly jobs gains over the past six and twelve months is about 80,000, the overall labor market remains in a broadly balanced state, with no significant deterioration. This means the Fed, faced with persistently high inflation, need not worry about the impact of rate hikes on jobs as much as it would if the labor market were visibly weakening. Brian Jacobsen, Chief Economic Strategist at Annex Wealth Management, pointed out from a price transmission angle that three consecutive months of core CPI rising 0.3% month-on-month shows that the issue isn’t just high headline CPI, but that energy shocks may have begun to seep into core inflation. He also mentioned that Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee previously discussed how AI demand could be a new source of inflationary pressure for the Fed. As AI investment and infrastructure expansion rise, economic activity may crowd out resources in other areas and push up prices for some services. Jacobsen suggests the Fed may increasingly focus on the resource squeeze from AI demand and rising wage costs for skilled trades like plumbers and electricians. Jeff Schulze, Chief Investment Strategist at Franklin Templeton Institute, warned that the latest inflation data will serve as a headwind for risk assets. Investors are beginning to price in a 50-basis-point December hike and more afterward; rising short-term yields and a stronger US dollar could both suppress equity valuations. Karen Manna, Fixed Income Investment Strategist at Federated Hermes, also said the report strengthens the rationale for another Fed rate hike and further demands policymakers maintain vigilance. The real concern for investors is that if inflation remains high, the Fed may have to keep monetary policy restrictive for an extended period, well into 2027. Overall, the October CPI brings a December rate hike closer to market consensus, but the policy options facing the Fed are no longer just whether to raise rates. Waller’s 50-basis-point option, Timiraos’ comments on rate-hike spacing, and whether other officials will support speeding up the pace of tightening—all will be key market focuses going forward.

item.title: CPI Deals a Blow to US Bonds! 2-Year Yield Surges Over 20 Basis Points Intraday, Gold and Silver Plunge
item.description: After the release of the CPI, traders began to expect a lower likelihood of a 50 basis point rate hike in December; this year’s Federal Reserve voting member Logan stated that a faster pace of rate hikes may be needed this winter, with at least two more 25 basis point hikes required before pausing. Subsequently, the rise in U.S. Treasury yields continued to widen, with the 10-year yield climbing back above 5.0% and rising more than 10 basis points intraday; spot gold once fell over 3%, while spot silver at one point dropped more than 4%.
item.dc:creator: 华尔街见闻
item.content:encoded: In October, U.S. inflation once again exceeded market expectations, triggering a sell-off in U.S. Treasury bonds and a sharp rise in yields across the board. The strengthening U.S. dollar and heightened expectations for higher interest rates also put pressure on gold and silver. With Federal Reserve officials repeatedly sending hawkish signals, markets are not only increasingly betting on a rate hike in December but are also beginning to assess the possibility of a larger hike and further monetary policy tightening into next year. On Tuesday, U.S. Eastern Time, after the release of the U.S. CPI data, U.S. Treasuries were heavily sold, sending prices plunging and yields accelerating higher. The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield expanded its gains following the CPI release and, after remarks by Federal Reserve official Lorie Logan, briefly broke above 5.01% during the U.S. stock market midday session, rising more than 10 basis points on the day. The 2-year Treasury yield, which is more sensitive to Fed policy expectations, climbed even more, surpassing 4.77% during midday and jumping more than 20 basis points on the day, on course for its biggest single-day surge since April last year. Precious metals markets also came under pressure. After the U.S. CPI release, gold extended its losses during the session. In the U.S. stock market midday, New York gold futures hit an intraday low of $4,020.8 per ounce, dropping nearly 2.3% on the day; spot gold fell below $4,014 per ounce, down nearly 3.1% intraday. The decline in silver was even more pronounced. Market data shows that at the day's lows in New York's midday, silver futures fell nearly 3% intraday, while spot silver plunged over 4%. CPI Inflation Continues to Beat Expectations for Months, Bond Market Reprices Fed Policy Path The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on Tuesday that October CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month, higher than the market expectation of 0.3%, but slowed from 0.6% in September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy prices, also rose 0.3% month-on-month, surpassing expectations of 0.2% and matching September’s increase. This marks the third consecutive month of 0.3% gains for core CPI. Due to the U.S. federal government shutdown at the same time last year, which prevented data collection, the Bureau did not release year-on-year CPI data for October. Just hours before the CPI data was released, the market was already rattled by hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller. In a speech in London on Tuesday, Waller said that even if inflation improved in October, he would still be inclined to support a 25 basis point Fed rate hike in December. However, if core CPI reached 0.3% or higher for a third straight month, the Fed should consider a 50 basis point hike in December. He warned that raising rates by only 25 basis points could undermine the credibility of the Fed’s fight against inflation. The actual core CPI published hit Waller’s 0.3% threshold precisely. After the data release, markets quickly ramped up bets on a larger rate hike. Reuters reported that traders’ implied probability of a 50 basis point hike by the Fed in December spiked to about 13.6%, from near zero before the data was released; by contrast, a 25 basis point hike had already become the mainstream market expectation. According to Bloomberg, the inflation data triggered a sell-off in Treasuries, with short-term maturities bearing the brunt. Money markets also increased bets that the Fed will hike rates at least two more times by mid-2027, and began more clearly pricing in the possibility of a one-off 50 basis point hike in December. Lindsay Rosner, Head of Multi-Sector Fixed Income Investing at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, said that if CPI remains robust, the Fed may usher in a more aggressive tightening cycle. Her view reflects market worries over persistently high inflation: even if a December hike is now the baseline expectation, future policy rates could still be more hawkish than previously anticipated. This Year’s FOMC Voter Logan: Faster Rate Hikes May Be Needed This Winter, Fed Needs at Least Two More 25 Basis Point Hikes Before a Pause Following the CPI release, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan also sent further signals of policy tightening. Logan is a voting member of the FOMC this year. Speaking at an energy conference co-hosted by the Dallas Fed and the Kansas City Fed on Tuesday, she said that given current economic and inflation prospects, the Fed still needs to implement at least two additional 25 basis point hikes. Logan noted that the specific pace of hikes depends on the near-term economic and financial environment, and that the Fed might need to move faster this winter than it has this autumn. She stated, "It may be necessary this winter to act more quickly than the FOMC has so far this autumn." However, Logan is not advocating for continuous rate hikes. She said that after completing these two hikes, the Fed could pause to assess the economy and financial markets before deciding on further policy adjustments. She also emphasized that if inflation remains above target for an extended period, it could gradually become entrenched in business and household expectations, making timely action crucial. Logan’s comments signal that some Fed officials are discussing not just whether to hike rates in December, but also how to reach a moderately restrictive level more quickly. Her statements echoed Waller’s, further fueling market concerns about the Fed tightening policy even more over the coming months. U.S. Treasury Yields and Dollar Rise Together, Doubling Pressure on Gold and Silver Both U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar are strengthening, putting pressure on non-yielding precious metals. On one hand, higher bond yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets like gold and silver; on the other hand, a stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated precious metals more expensive for holders of other currencies. According to Reuters, after October inflation data came in higher than expected, gold prices fell noticeably as the market began evaluating the chances of the Fed taking a more aggressive rate-hiking stance. Gold is especially sensitive to changes in interest rate expectations, and if the market further raises its outlook for policy rates, precious metals could continue to face pressure in the short term. However, the future path for gold and silver will not depend solely on Fed policy. Movements in the dollar, geopolitical risks, energy prices, and investors’ outlook on the economy can all affect demand for precious metals. The key market shift currently is that both the inflation data and hawkish comments from Fed officials have reinforced expectations for higher rates, forcing a reset in precious metals trades that previously benefited from rate-cut expectations.

Nov 10 : Australia's Marnus Labuschagne said on Tuesday he remains confident about returning to the test side after selectors left him out of next month's four-test home series against New Zealand following a prolonged slump in form. • The 32-year-old number three, once the world's top-ranked test batter, has gone 49 innings without a century and endured another poor tour of South Africa, scoring zero and four in the final test as Australia lost the match and series 2-1. • "I've got no doubt I will be back there. When? Who knows," Labuschagne told reporters. • "I think my path back into the Australia team will work itself out. I've done it before. It's something that I truly want." • Labuschagne has averaged 23.66 and managed only two half-centuries in 10 tests since being dropped for the three-test series against West Indies in the Caribbean last year.

MADRID, Nov 10 : Spain's government has demanded that TikTok suspend its operations in Spain until it eliminates child sexual abuse material, it said on Tuesday, after a media report documented 1,183 explicit posts on the platform with millions of views. Youth Minister Sira Rego, whose ministry cannot singlehandedly ban the platform in Spain, has appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency to take action against the social media company, according to a statement by the ministry. "Social media cannot be lawless territory," Rego said. The request comes months after Sanchez's government requested a probe into X, Meta and TikTok for allegedly spreading AI-generated child sexual abuse material, as European regulators intensify scrutiny of big tech over harmful and illegal content.

TikTok did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Spanish fact-checking nonprofit Maldita.es on Monday published an investigation revealing that videos of explicit child sexual abuse had been viewed on the platform at least 48 million times, with over 26,000 profiles commenting on and sharing the material. The organisation published a follow-up story on Tuesday evening stating that TikTok had restricted two of the search terms that Maldita.es's investigation identified as pathways to child sexual abuse content for users in Spain, but that searches from other European countries still led to the same content.

item.title: Fed’s Christopher Waller opens door to 50-basis-point December rate hike after hot CPI
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point December rate hike after US core inflation rose 0.3% in October. Persistent price pressures have intensified debate over tighter monetary policy and the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility.
item.dc:creator: ETMarkets.com
item.content:encoded: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller's remarks intensified the debate over a possible half-percentage-point interest-rate increase in December after US inflation data came in hotter than expected on Tuesday, Bloomberg reported.In a speech delivered in London before the release of October’s Consumer Price Index, Waller said he was inclined to support a rate increase in December. He warned that a 50-basis-point move might be necessary if inflation continued to accelerate, arguing that the Fed’s credibility could otherwise be at risk.Hours later, data showed that consumer prices rose more than expected. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, increased 0.3% from the previous month, meeting the threshold Waller identified as grounds for considering a larger rate increase.Also read: Traders raise odds of 50 bps Fed rate hike as CPI rise exceeds expectationsWaller’s remarks represent the clearest signal yet from a Fed official that policymakers may need to raise rates in December by more than the quarter-percentage-point move markets had expected.Several senior Fed officials, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams, are scheduled to speak this week.Fed watchers said Waller’s comments did not make a 50-basis-point move certain but would add urgency to the debate over how aggressively policymakers must act to contain inflation.“This is not a print that screams out the need to go 50, but certainly provides ammunition to the argument to do so,” Christopher Hodge, chief US economist at Natixis, told Bloomberg.For live updates on US Markets, click hereTom Porcelli, chief economist at Wells Fargo, said he expected the Fed’s policy-setting committee to support another rate increase unanimously, although the size of the move remained open for debate.“This locks it down,” Porcelli said, referring to the likelihood of at least a 25-basis-point increase. “With Waller introducing that idea, the market is going to run with it in the face of this firm print.”Following Waller’s remarks and the inflation report, investors priced in a more aggressive path for interest rates in the coming months. However, markets remained unconvinced that policymakers would deliver a half-point increase in December.Federal funds futures continued to indicate a quarter-point move in December, followed by additional increases of the same size in January and possibly April. Investors had previously expected rate increases in December and March.Waller described the US economy as strong and the labour market as stable but said inflation remained too high.“If, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points,” Waller said.“But if the October CPI inflation data out later today are similar to the past two monthly readings—with core CPI inflation around 0.3% or even higher—then a stronger policy move may be needed,” he added. “In that case, I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting.”Under such a scenario, Waller said a conventional quarter-point increase would do little to reassure the public that the Fed was serious about controlling inflation.“Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take,” he said.Also Read: Are days of easy money over? Aswath Damodaran warns of a new mkt realityHot CPI intensifies rate debateData released later by the Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October from the previous month, while the headline CPI increased 0.4%.Fed officials held interest rates steady last month, saying the “accumulation of more information” would help them determine the appropriate policy setting.The 10-2 decision followed a unanimous vote in September to raise the benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4%. Several policymakers have since indicated that additional increases may be necessary.Data released last week showed that job growth accelerated in October while the unemployment rate edged lower. Fed officials will receive another employment report and a full set of inflation data before their December meeting.During a question-and-answer session with Bloomberg’s Francine Lacqua after the speech, Waller said the Fed did not want to “slam the economy down.”“It’s not that we’re going to jack up the policy rate 150 basis points or 200 basis points,” he said. “We are looking forward and saying we need to do something; at a minimum, probably take back the three insurance cuts that we put in last year.”Waller added that monetary policy had not been “nearly as restrictive as I thought it was.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 10 : US electricity consumption will rise to record highs in 2026 and 2027 due to power-hungry AI data centers and electrification, the US Energy Information Administration said in its Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO) on Tuesday. The EIA projected that power demand will rise from a record 4,216 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) in 2025 to 4,306 billion kWh in 2026 and 4,370 billion kWh in 2027. If correct, 2026 would be the third year in a row of record demand. Demand is surging largely due to data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence. Homes and businesses have also been relying more on electricity and less on fossil fuels for heat and transportation. The EIA forecast that power sales in 2026 will rise to 1,546 billion kWh for residential consumers, 1,557 billion kWh for commercial customers and 1,061 billion kWh for industrial customers.

The all-time highs stand at 1,519 billion kWh for residential consumers and 1,503 billion kWh for commercial customers in 2025 and 1,064 billion kWh for industrial customers in 2000. As renewable output rises, the EIA said the share of power generation from coal will slide from 17 per cent in 2025 to 15 per cent in 2026 and 2027, while the share of natural gas in 2026 will hold steady from 2025 at 40 per cent, then ease to 39 per cent in 2027. The percentage of renewable generation will rise from around 24 per cent in 2025 to 25 per cent in 2026 and 28 per cent in 2027, while nuclear power's share will hold at 18 per cent in 2026 and 2027, the same as in 2025, according to the outlook. The EIA projected that gas sales in 2026 would slide to 12.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) for residential consumers and 9.4 bcfd for commercial customers, but rise to 23.8 bcfd for industrial customers and 37.4 bcfd for power generation. Those figures compare with all-time highs of 14.3 bcfd in 1996 for residential consumers, 9.9 bcfd in 2025 for commercial customers, 23.8 bcfd in 1973 for industrial customers, and 36.8 bcfd in 2024 for power generation.

Source: Reuters

Nov 10 : Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev are the first players confirmed to represent Europe at the 2027 Laver Cup in Los Angeles, organisers announced on Tuesday, as the team bids for a record-extending seventh title. The 10th edition of the tournament will take place at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles from September 24-26. Team World is made up of players from outside Europe. The annual tournament, launched in 2017, is intended to be tennis's equivalent of golf's Ryder Cup. World number one Zverev will make a record eighth Laver Cup appearance in Los Angeles, having been part of Team Europe's six title-winning campaigns since making his debut at the inaugural event in Prague in 2017.

The German delivered the decisive points in this year's 13-5 victory over Team World in London and also sealed triumphs in Chicago in 2018, Geneva in 2019 and Boston in 2021, when he teamed up with Andrey Rublev in the doubles. "I've been part of Laver Cup since the very beginning and it's become one of my favourite weeks of the year," Zverev said in a statement. Alcaraz will make his fourth consecutive appearance after debuting in Berlin in 2024, where he beat Taylor Fritz to secure the title. "I’m really happy to be coming back for my fourth Laver Cup and to be playing alongside Sascha again,” Alcaraz added.

item.title: NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China
item.description: NVDA shares fell 4.43% to $170.75 as of 9:53 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 10, after The Information reported that Jensen Huang's personal relationship with a businesswoman alleged to work ...
item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China

NVIDIA Stocks Slide 4.43% as Report Alleges $7.5 Billion in Chips Reached China 1 min read

NVDA NVIDIA NVDA shares fell 4.43% to $170.75 as of 9:53 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 10, after The Information reported that Jensen Huang's personal relationship with a businesswoman alleged to work for Beijing helped move at least $7.5 billion of its chips to Chinese firms. That stacks on Monday's 4.27% drop. Reuters, which carried the report, said it could not independently verify the claims. The report describes a web of companies in China and Singapore, centered on Shanghai Century Litong, that won preferred cloud-partner status within months of its June 2023 founding. When orders for export-restricted chips stalled, roughly 240,000 H100, H200 and A100 units allegedly reached China. Some of that capacity reportedly served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs. The company's board said a committee of independent directors with outside counsel is running the review. The board added that it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

From the November 6 close of $186.64, the two-day slide is 8.51%, roughly $383 billion of market value on about 24.1 billion shares. The GuruFocus profile is lopsided: GF Score 92/100, Profitability 10/10, Financial Strength 9/10 and Momentum 10/10, but GF Value Rank only 2/10. At $170.75 the shares trade 60.10% below the $427.93 GF Value, yet GuruFocus itself tags the setup "Possible Value Trap, Think Twice." The model gap alone is no bargain signal. The next hard test is the November 17 third-quarter report, where any export-control questions would surface in guidance or disclosures.

item.title: Bolsa Mexicana espera nuevas emisiones de acciones en 2027: qué falta para atraer capital
item.description: Representantes de BlackRock, Vanguard, la BMV y Bitso analizaron los desafíos de liquidez, regulación y acceso a la inversión durante el Bloomberg Línea Summit México 2026.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rodríguez Salcedo
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — La Bolsa Mexicana de Valores (BMV) espera concretar emisiones simplificadas de acciones en 2027, una de las oportunidades para impulsar el mercado de capitales mexicano, cuyos retos de liquidez, regulación y acceso a la inversión marcaron el debate durante el Bloomberg Línea Summit México 2026 . Ver más: Cinco razones por las que Wall Street puede seguir subiendo en los últimos meses de 2026 El objetivo forma parte de los esfuerzos de la industria financiera para ampliar el acceso al mercado de capitales, atraer nuevas empresas y superar los obstáculos de liquidez, regulación y participación de inversionistas. El panel reunió a Sergio Méndez, de BlackRock México ( BLK ); Juan Hernández, de Vanguard; Jorge Alegría, de la BMV, y Felipe Vallejo, de Bitso México. “Estamos esperando que sí”, respondió Alegría al ser consultado sobre la posibilidad de concretar emisiones simplificadas de acciones en 2027, después de que la bolsa completara su primera operación de deuda bajo este mecanismo. La financiera no bancaria Adventus Capital realizó el 7 de octubre la primera emisión simplificada de deuda de la BMV, por MXN$560 millones (US$31 millones). La operación se completó en cinco semanas, frente a los seis meses que habría requerido un proceso tradicional. La BMV tiene en marcha un proceso confidencial de listado de una empresa que busca emitir acciones bajo el esquema simplificado. Este mecanismo agiliza las colocaciones y está reservado a inversionistas institucionales y calificados. La diferencia entre ambos segmentos es significativa. Mientras el mercado de deuda mexicano acumulaba más de MXN$580.000 millones en financiamiento durante 2026, las nuevas colocaciones accionarias continuaban limitadas. Suscríbete al newsletter Línea de Mercado , una selección de Bloomberg Línea con las noticias bursátiles más destacadas del día. Alegría sostuvo que “tenemos que aumentar mucho más la liquidez de las acciones que ya existen”, una condición que considera necesaria para fortalecer la confianza de los inversionistas mexicanos. El crecimiento de la demanda también depende de los incentivos para canalizar recursos hacia instrumentos de largo plazo, según Sergio Méndez, de BlackRock México, quien planteó revisar aspectos fiscales y regulatorios. Méndez destacó el préstamo de valores como una herramienta que puede contribuir a incrementar la liquidez y mejorar las condiciones de operación del mercado. La industria de fondos ofrece otra perspectiva sobre la evolución del ahorro financiero. Juan Hernández, de Vanguard, destacó que estos vehículos administran MXN$5,3 billones y acumulan aproximadamente 20 millones de cuentas. Hace 15 años, la exposición a renta variable y fondos multiactivos representaba apenas el 2% de la industria. Actualmente, la participación de estos instrumentos supera el 25%, según las cifras presentadas por Hernández. El Sistema Internacional de Cotizaciones (SIC) también ha ampliado las alternativas disponibles, con más de 4.000 valores, entre ellos cerca de 2.000 fondos cotizados en bolsa (ETF). Ver más: Exclusiva: CFE evalúa emisión por US$2.000 millones para Fibra con activos de generación eléctrica Sin embargo, el acceso a instrumentos internacionales contrasta con la necesidad de fortalecer la negociación de acciones mexicanas, particularmente entre inversionistas que ya participan en compañías extranjeras. La BMV busca que empresas como Bimbo ( BIMBOA ), FEMSA ( FEMSAUBD ), Televisa ( TLEVICPO ) y América Móvil ( AMXB ) despierten un interés comparable al que generan Tesla ( TSLA ), Amazon ( AMZN ) y otras compañías internacionales. La expansión de las plataformas digitales ha facilitado la apertura de cuentas bursátiles, pero el crecimiento del acceso no necesariamente se ha traducido en una mayor participación en acciones. Felipe Vallejo, de Bitso México, explicó que una encuesta entre clientes con activos en la plataforma encontró que solamente el 10% había invertido en bolsa, ya fuera mexicana o internacional. Para la compañía, la oportunidad consiste en facilitar la distribución de productos financieros y reducir las barreras que todavía separan a los usuarios digitales de los mercados bursátiles. “Creo que solo falta hacerlo bien, bien fácil”, afirmó Vallejo al referirse a la experiencia que necesitan los inversionistas minoristas. Ver más: Emisión simplificada en Bolsa Mexicana despertó interés para más listados en deuda y acciones: CEO La disponibilidad de servicios fuera del horario bancario es otro factor. Según Bitso, un tercio del volumen de su servicio de inversión Invierto se registra cuando las instituciones financieras tradicionales no están abiertas. La compañía considera que los horarios extendidos responden a los hábitos de personas que revisan sus inversiones después de concluir su jornada laboral. La BMV también contempla ampliar sus horarios de negociación. Actualmente, determinados productos derivados ya operan durante sesiones extendidas, mientras la infraestructura tecnológica se prepara para nuevas modalidades. No obstante, la ampliación exige coordinación entre bancos, intermediarios, sistemas de liquidación y autoridades, además de la capacidad tecnológica de las plataformas. La bolsa desarrolla una modernización de sus sistemas de negociación, custodia y posnegociación, con tecnología de Nasdaq y cambios en la infraestructura de Indeval. La primera etapa está prevista para 2027 y la última para 2028. El proyecto también busca integrar información que actualmente se encuentra distribuida entre diferentes plataformas y entidades del mercado. Ver más: Financiera Adventus Capital realiza la primera emisión simplificada de deuda en la Bolsa Mexicana La disponibilidad de datos permitiría desarrollar herramientas para analistas, inversionistas y sistemas de inteligencia artificial, además de mejorar los procesos de información y supervisión. El acceso tecnológico, sin embargo, representa solamente una parte del desafío. Vanguard identificó la asesoría financiera como uno de los principales espacios pendientes de desarrollo. Hernández estimó que México cuenta con entre 9.000 y 10.000 asesores de inversión para una población cercana a 130 millones de habitantes, una proporción reducida frente a otros mercados. Como referencia, señaló que Brasil pasó de aproximadamente 5.000 a 30.000 asesores durante los últimos seis años, mientras Estados Unidos dispone de unos 300.000 profesionales. La digitalización podría reducir el costo de la asesoría y facilitar el acceso a servicios que tradicionalmente requieren patrimonios elevados. Aun así, Vanguard considera que las herramientas automatizadas no sustituyen por completo la relación con un asesor, especialmente cuando las personas deben tomar decisiones patrimoniales relevantes. Ver más: Bonos de Venezuela enfrentan riesgo de más pérdidas: la alerta de una consultora de EE.UU. Méndez, de BlackRock, insistió en que la educación financiera debe acompañar la expansión de las plataformas, particularmente para evitar decisiones motivadas por movimientos de corto plazo. “Invertir es un proceso de generación de rendimientos de largo plazo”, sostuvo durante su intervención. La diversificación también ocupó un lugar central en la discusión. Vanguard destacó que la asignación entre acciones, bonos, divisas y otros instrumentos explica una proporción importante del comportamiento de los portafolios. Hernández resumió los principios de inversión de la administradora en planificación, diversificación, control de costos y disciplina para mantener una estrategia durante episodios de volatilidad. La transformación del mercado mexicano también estará condicionada por tendencias internacionales, entre ellas la inteligencia artificial, la fragmentación geopolítica y los cambios demográficos. BlackRock identificó oportunidades relacionadas con infraestructura tecnológica, centros de datos, semiconductores y necesidades de financiamiento para sostener la expansión de nuevas capacidades productivas. Ver más: Goldman Sachs recorta su previsión para el precio del oro: ¿cuál es su proyección para 2027? Méndez consideró que “la necesidad de capital en el mundo para financiar este cambio económico es otra realidad”, en referencia a la magnitud de las inversiones requeridas por las grandes compañías tecnológicas. La reorganización de las cadenas de suministro y la consolidación de bloques económicos también forman parte de las tendencias identificadas por la administradora. En particular, BlackRock destacó las oportunidades asociadas con Norteamérica, aunque reconoció que las tensiones políticas pueden introducir incertidumbre en las decisiones de inversión. Vanguard comparó la expansión de la inteligencia artificial con transformaciones históricas de infraestructura, por la magnitud del gasto de capital destinado a centros de datos y capacidad tecnológica. Hernández planteó un escenario de crecimiento de Estados Unidos cercano al 3%, impulsado por la inversión tecnológica, aunque advirtió sobre la importancia de que ese gasto se traduzca en productividad. La discusión también abordó el envejecimiento de la población y la disminución de las tasas de fecundidad, factores que podrían modificar las necesidades de inversión y las perspectivas económicas. Ver más: Una guía para invertir tras resultados de elecciones en EE.UU.: acciones, bonos, dólar y oro Desde Bitso, Vallejo destacó la relación entre los cambios demográficos y la inteligencia artificial, particularmente por sus posibles efectos sobre la productividad. En el terreno financiero, la compañía distinguió entre el desarrollo de las stablecoins y los mercados de predicción, dos segmentos que atraviesan etapas regulatorias diferentes. Las monedas estables ya tienen aplicaciones en pagos internacionales y remesas. En México, Bitso destacó su utilización para transferencias transfronterizas, mientras en Argentina identificó una demanda vinculada al resguardo de valor. “Ya el mundo está regulando esto y ya lo está usando”, afirmó Vallejo al referirse al avance internacional de las stablecoins . Los mercados de predicción, por su parte, mantienen interrogantes regulatorios, especialmente sobre su clasificación como instrumentos financieros o mecanismos de apuestas. Aunque Bitso identificó posibles aplicaciones para cobertura de riesgos, consideró necesario evaluar su funcionamiento y sus efectos antes de impulsar una regulación específica en México. Ver más: Soja, trigo y fertilizantes: Banco Mundial prevé más presión sobre el precio de los alimentos La tokenización también apareció entre las alternativas futuras del mercado, aunque tanto la BMV como Bitso coincidieron en priorizar la infraestructura, la liquidez y la digitalización. En materia regulatoria, la bolsa identificó el préstamo de valores, las operaciones de reporto y la liquidación de derivados como prioridades para mejorar el funcionamiento del mercado. Alegría sostuvo que estos cambios podrían tener efectos importantes sobre la negociación bursátil, incluso sin necesidad de reformas estructurales de mayor alcance. Para Bitso, otra oportunidad consiste en orientar parte de la inclusión financiera hacia productos de inversión y financiamiento para empresas, en lugar de concentrarla en el crédito al consumo. El avance de estas iniciativas dependerá de las autorizaciones regulatorias, la adopción tecnológica y la respuesta de los inversionistas, mientras la BMV prepara sus siguientes etapas de modernización y nuevas colocaciones para 2027.
